thread.title: Slowing China takes a bite out of Apple’s forecasts By INCE|Connect

author: INCE|Connect
title: Slowing China takes a bite out of Apple’s forecasts By INCE|Connect
text:
© Reuters. The company's downward sales revision stunned the market, sending its shares sharply lower.
Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL )'s shares fell 9% in after-hours trading after the group cut its quarterly sales forecast for the first time since 2007. The move sent US stock futures into the red. The group blamed a downturn in iPhone sales in China, which makes up nearly a fifth of the group's revenue. It now expects to report revenue for the first quarter to end-December of $84 billion, down from an earlier projection of $91 billion.
In a letter to investors, CEO Tim Cook said first-quarter sales had also been affected by the release of its iPhone Xs and iPhone Xs Max models, which shipped in the fourth quarter of its previous financial year. Last year its iPhone X shipped in the first quarter. It said the strong US dollar had also affected foreign exchange revenue growth. In addition, it faced constraints in the supply of its Apple Watch Series 4 and iPad Pro and economic weakness in some emerging markets, which had a bigger impact than expected. This resulted in fewer iPhone upgrades than anticipated.
While we anticipated some challenges in key emerging markets, we did not foresee the magnitude of the economic deceleration, particularly in Greater China,"," Apple CEO Tim Cook said in a letter to investors. "In fact, most of our revenue shortfall to our guidance, and over 100 percent of our year-over-year worldwide revenue decline occurred in Greater China across iPhone, Mac and iPad."
Apple said its future in China remained "bright", with its products enjoying a strong following among customers, with a very high level of engagement and satisfaction. While its revenue shortfall for the period could be attributed to lower than anticipated iPhone revenue from Greater China, it said other categories including services, Mac, iPad, and Wearables/Home/Accessories combined to grow almost 19% year-on-year.
The group expects to exit the quarter with about $130 billion in net cash
